_description: 0-day and exploit marketplace activity on Telegram. Rules use multi-signal lookahead regex (require BOTH a target term AND a transaction/context term) to suppress vendor advisories, security news, defender chatter, and CTF/learning content. See examples/threat-packs/README.md for detection logic and known FP risks.

rules._description: Direct sale offer: someone is offering a private exploit or 0-day. Requires BOTH (1) an exploit/0-day term AND (2) a transactional signal - sale verb, pricing language, escrow, contact-ask, or crypto payment. Excludes vendor-advisory and defender-discussion phrasing.
rules._fp_risk: Medium-low. Will fire on roleplay/scam offers (which is actually OK - those are still TI signals). Tune excludes if your corpus contains many CTF/training channels.
rules._severity_rationale: Critical - confirmed sale intent for offensive capability.
rules.name: 0day - direct sale offer

rules._description: Chatter about exploits for high-impact products - anything mentioning a critical attack primitive (preauth RCE, sandbox escape, kernel exploit, 0-click, hypervisor escape, jailbreak) against a high-value product (major browsers, edge appliances, hypervisors, popular enterprise apps). Two-signal lookahead: product term + critical primitive term.
rules._fp_risk: Medium. CVE-assigned + patched issues will fire unless the excludes catch the vendor/news framing. Tune the excludes if you ingest many security-news channels.
rules._severity_rationale: Critical - even chatter (not yet for sale) about working exploits for these targets is high-priority TI.
rules.name: 0day - high-impact product chatter

rules._description: Buyer-side: exploit brokers or actors soliciting private exploits. Two-signal lookahead: explicit buy/acquire/payout intent + exploit/0-day target term. Recognizes commercial broker names (Crowdfense, Trenchant, etc.) as additional hits.
rules._fp_risk: Medium. Bug bounty platforms use overlapping language ('we pay up to'). Excludes pin platform names (HackerOne, Bugcrowd) since they are NOT underground. Adjust if you want broker activity from those platforms tracked separately.
rules._severity_rationale: High - broker activity signals demand; not as actionable as a confirmed sale but worth tracking.
rules.name: 0day - exploit broker / acquisition

rules._description: Public weaponization: PoC released, exploit code dropped, or in-the-wild exploitation reported. Two-signal lookahead: release/ITW language + CVE/product target. This is distinct from .direct-sale (here the artifact is public, not for sale).
rules._fp_risk: Low-medium. Will fire on legitimate research drops (e.g. Project Zero). Excludes catch CTF/training/course content. Defenders may want this anyway - it's actionable for patching prioritization.
rules._severity_rationale: High - public PoC dramatically lowers attacker skill bar; ITW = active exploitation.
rules.name: 0day - public PoC / ITW

rules._description: 0-click / zero-interaction exploit chatter - typically iMessage, WhatsApp, Outlook, Teams. These are the highest-value mobile/messaging exploits (Pegasus-class). Single-signal regex by design - zero-click language alone is rare enough to justify alerting.
rules._fp_risk: Low. 'Zero-click' is rare jargon outside actual research/intel discussion. Excludes catch news framing.
rules._severity_rationale: Critical - zero-click capability is at the top of the exploit value pyramid.
rules.name: 0day - 0-click exploit chatter
